test.title: guest can add a product to the cart
test.error:
Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.')
Expected: visible

triage.reason: The test navigated, opened the product, and successfully clicked the Add to cart button (the failure is at line 8, not 6 or 7), so the page structure the spec relies on is intact and the action was performed. The only thing missing is the app's success confirmation, and it was missing on all 3 attempts after a full 5s of polling, which rules out flakiness. The most likely cause is that the app failed to confirm/perform the add-to-cart. The alternative — that the toast wording changed, making the string stale — is possible but unsupported, since every other locator in the flow still matched; it keeps confidence at medium.
triage.evidence: "Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed / Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.') / Error: element(s) not found" occurring only after line 7 "await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();" succeeded, with "Status: failed on every attempt (3 attempts)".
triage.next_step: Open the Playwright trace/screenshot for the failed attempt at line 8 and inspect the network request fired by the Add to cart click: if the cart POST returns an error or no request is sent, it is an app bug; if it succeeds but a differently worded toast appears, update the expected string in the test.

>  9 |   await expect(page.getByText('There are no products found.')).toBeVisible();
     |                                                                ^
  10 | });
  11 |
    at tests\products-mock.spec.ts:9:64

triage.reason: Deterministic failure on all 3 attempts rules out flakiness. The test depends entirely on its own mock, and the mock is the weak link: `page.route('**/products', ...)` matches the full URL, so a real request carrying a query string (e.g. `/products?page=0&between=price,1,100`) is never intercepted. The real, non-empty product list then renders and the empty-state text legitimately never appears — matching "element(s) not found". Nothing in the log proves the route fired, so there is no evidence the empty-state element should have been on the page; per the locator rule this points at the test, not the app. A stale expected string or a payload envelope (`{ data: [] }`) the app doesn't parse would also be test-side defects. A genuine app bug in rendering the empty state remains possible but is unsupported until the mock is shown to take effect, hence medium confidence.
triage.evidence: Mock setup: `await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));` with the assumption in the comment "it never reaches the server"; failure: "Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed / Locator: getByText('There are no products found.') / Error: element(s) not found".
triage.next_step: Add `page.on('request', r => console.log(r.url()))` (or check the trace's Network tab) to capture the actual products request URL; if it carries a query string, widen the mock to `**/products?**` or a regex like `/\/products(\?|$)/`, re-run, and confirm the rendered empty-state copy matches 'There are no products found.' exactly.

triage.reason: Only the error text and the test snippet are available (no shell/file access in this session to inspect the app markup, config, or trace), and the evidence fits two causes about equally well. (1) Broken script: `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' })` never resolved at all — the call log shows only "waiting for getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' })" with no retry/strictness message, which is the classic signature of an accessible-name/role mismatch (e.g. the real input is named "Search for products" or has only a placeholder/`data-test="search-query"` with no accessible name), i.e. the page changed or the locator is wrong. (2) Real bug: the same timeout would occur if `page.goto('/')` landed on a broken or empty home page so the search box genuinely never rendered. Rule 4 says an unmatched locator is normally a broken script, but failing on all 3 attempts at the very first interaction — before any app assertion — leaves a broken home page equally plausible, and nothing in the evidence shows the element was present. Timing/flakiness is ruled out: it failed identically on every one of 3 attempts.
triage.evidence: Error line: "Error: locator.fill: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' })" against code line 6: `await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' }).fill('Pliers');` — the locator matched nothing for the full 30s. Note the hint's alternative ("matched more than one") is contradicted by the call log, which shows no strict-mode violation.
triage.next_step: Open the failed run's trace/screenshot for tests/search.spec.ts:6 (`npx playwright show-trace`) and inspect the home page DOM snapshot: if the search input is present, read its actual role/accessible name and fix the locator (e.g. `getByPlaceholder('Search')` or `[data-test="search-query"]`) — broken script; if the home page rendered empty or errored on `goto('/')`, file it as a real bug.

test.title: Filtering by a single category shows only that category's products
test.error:
Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
  13 |
test.fullError:
Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.

Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.

  13 |
  14 |   // Step 2: select the category filter. The shop sends the filter as a QUERY request to /products.
> 15 |   const filterResponse = page.waitForResponse(
     |                               ^
  16 |     (response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products'),
  17 |   );
  18 |   await homePage.filter(CATEGORY).check();
    at tests\TOOL-4-TC-1.spec.ts:15:31

triage.reason: The test waits for a response whose request method is the exotic HTTP verb 'QUERY'. Chromium-driven page code (fetch/XHR) does not issue 'QUERY' requests, and product filtering is conventionally a GET (or POST) to /products, so this predicate can never be satisfied and the wait must time out. That matches the deterministic failure on all 3 attempts, while everything before it worked: the page loaded, products were visible, and the filter checkbox was located and checked (the error is on the promise created at line 15, not on the click at line 18). Nothing in the evidence suggests the app failed to filter — the test aborted before any UI or payload assertion ran. The stale assumption is even written into the comment on line 14.
triage.evidence: Predicate: `(response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')` — failing with `Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.` at tests\TOOL-4-TC-1.spec.ts:15:31, with the comment "The shop sends the filter as a QUERY request to /products."
triage.next_step: Open DevTools (or run the test with `--trace on` and inspect the network tab of the trace) while checking the "Pliers" filter, note the real method and URL of the /products call, and relax the predicate accordingly (e.g. drop the method check and match on `response.url().includes('/products')` plus the category query parameter).

triage.reason: The test hangs in waitForResponse because its response predicate cannot match a normal filter request. It requires an HTTP method of 'QUERY' and a URL ending exactly in '/products', while shop filters are conventionally sent as 'GET /products?by_category=...', which fails both conditions. The click on line 18 raised no locator error, so the checkbox was interacted with successfully and only the network matcher failed, and the failure repeated identically on all 3 attempts, which excludes timing/flakiness.
